key_insight: PRIMS embeds fluid physics directly into a multimodal Transformer, making fluid identification more accurate, interpretable, and robust to changing operating conditions.
engineering_relevance: The method is well-suited for on-device microfluidic sensing where reliability must hold across variable flow, pressure, and temperature.
method: Physics-based Token Vectorization turns Coriolis and pressure signals into physically meaningful embeddings.
Physical Component Synthesizer models viscosity-related links among flow, pressure, and density.
Physics-guided Fusion uses attention to combine cross-physical correlations in the final representation.
evidence_signal: On a five-fluid benchmark, PRIMS reached 98.92% average F1 with 0.46M parameters and outperformed prior methods under unseen temperature and flow-rate shifts.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the embedded physical assumptions, so calibration and sensor-specific adaptation could still be needed in new hardware setups.
paper_title: PRIMS: Physics-guided Representation for Fluid Identification in Multimodal Sensing
